a:r.a:t: Dysfunction in Ganglioside Recycling Leads to a Variety of Medical Disorders

p:cNvPr.descr: Breakdown of various polar lipids to ceramide, as well as the associated diseases. To the right of the diagram is a box containing a key that shows the associated shapes and colors of various sugar residues: Glc = blue circle; GalNAc = yellow square; Gal = yellow circle; Neu5Ac = purple diamond. The diagram begins at the top left with a GM1 (labeled on the right). It is composed of a ceramide (represented by text in a box on the left) bonded right to Glc, bonded right to Gal, which bonds up to Neu5Ac and right to GalNAc, which bonds right to Gal. A down arrow is labeled on the left with blue text reading, "beta-galactosidase," the enzyme involved in moving to the next phase. There is a divergent right arrow with a yellow circle next to it, indicating removal of Gal. To the right there is also a circled red X with an arrow; to the right of this is text reading "generalized gangliosidosis" in an orange box. The down arrow then points to the same GM1 molecule, but this time the end Gal is removed. It is now labeled "GM2" at the right. A down arrow has blue text on the left reading, "hexoaminidase A;" on the right there is a circled red X with an arrow pointing right to an orange box with text reading "Tay-Sachs disease." There is a divergent arrow next to a yellow square, indicating the loss of GalNAc. The next image down shows GM3 (labeled right); the GM1 that now has Gal and GalNAc removed. A down arrow has blue text to its left reading, "ganglioside neuraminidase;" a divergent right arrow has a purple diamond next to it, showing the loss of Neu5Ac. Below this, the ceramide is now bonded right to only a Glc, which is bonded right to a single Gal. A down arrow is labeled with blue text on the left side reading, "beta-galactosidase;" a divergent arrow to the right has a yellow circle next to it, showing the loss of a second Gal. Below this the ceramide is now bonded only to a single Glc, to the right. A down arrow has blue text to its left reading, "glucocerebrosidase." To the right is a red circled X with an orange box containing text reading, "Gaucher disease." A divergent right arrow has a blue circle next to it, showing the loss of the Glc. Below, the ceramide is left unbonded. To the right is globoside, which consists of the ceramide on the left bonded right to Glc, which bonds right to Gal, which bonds right to Gal, which bonds right to GalNAc. A down arrow is labeled on the left with blue text reading, "hexosaminidase A and B," the enzyme involved in moving to the next phase. There is a divergent right arrow with a yellow square next to it, indicating removal of GalNAc. On the right there is a circled red X with an arrow pointing right to an orange box with text reading "Sandhoff Disease." The next molecule down is the same as described above, but it is missing a GalNAc. A down arrow is labeled "alpha-galactosidase A" in blue text; to the right there is a divergent arrow with a yellow circle next to it, showing the loss of a Gal. A circled red X to the right as an arrow that points to an orange box containing text reading, "Fabry disease." The down arrow turns left and meets with the ceramide bonded to a Glc and a Gal from the first reaction. At the bottom is a polar lipid labeled "sphingomyelin." It is a simple linkage of two boxes with text inside reading "ceramide" (left) and "phosphocholine" (right). A down arrow has blue text on the left side reading, "sphingomyelinase," with a divergent arrow and the phosphocholine box next to it. A circle red X to the right has an arrow pointing to an orange box with text reading, "Niemann-Pick disease." The down arrow then turns left and meets with the single ceramide box to the left.
